assays.assay_name: Open Field Test - Spontaneous locomotion & ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization (Experiment 1)
assays.assay_description: 10-min sessions in a circular wooden open-field arena (40 cm diameter, 50 cm high) with floor divided into 19 squares. Hand-counted locomotion frequency was measured for spontaneous activity (after ayahuasca alone), acute ethanol-induced hyperlocomotion (5 min post-ethanol, after ayahuasca or saline pretreatment), and a second ethanol challenge 7 days later to assess sensitization.

application_type.evidence: All solutions were given intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a volume of 10 ml/kg of body weight

setup_habituation.evidence: Eighty mice were given a 10-min habituation period in the open field on 2 consecutive days after a saline i.p. injection

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were placed in the open field for locomotion quantification (freely moving)

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (in home cage); no food in the open field apparatus

water_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum throughout the experiments (in home cage); no water in the open field apparatus

time_to_assay.evidence: Spontaneous locomotion: 30 min after ayahuasca. Acute ethanol: 5 min after ethanol. Sensitization test: 7 days later, 5 min after ethanol challenge.

sample_size.evidence: Six groups of animals were formed (n = 10 or 30); Sal n=30, Aya30-Aya500 n=10 each

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca (30-500 mg/kg) did not alter spontaneous locomotor activity. At 300 and 500 mg/kg, ayahuasca prevented acute ethanol-induced hyperlocomotion. At all doses tested, ayahuasca prevented the development of ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization measured one week later.
outcomes.statistics: Spontaneous: F(5,74)=0.41, p=0.83. Acute ethanol: F(6,73)=11.74, p<0.0001; Tukey p<0.05 for 300 and 500 mg/kg vs Sal-Eth. Sensitization: F(7,72)=7.87, p<0.0001; Tukey p<0.05.
outcomes.evidence: Ayahuasca did not modify spontaneous locomotor activity per se. At the doses of 300 and 500 mg/kg, ayahuasca prevented the acute stimulating effect of ethanol. Treatment with ayahuasca at all doses before the first ethanol administration prevented the development of ethanol-induced sensitization.

assays.assay_name: Open Field Test - Ethanol sensitization and counter-sensitization with ayahuasca (Experiment 2)
assays.assay_description: 10-min open-field sessions across a multi-phase protocol: habituation (days 1-2), ethanol sensitization phase (alternate days 3-17, locomotion recorded days 3 and 17), 8-day counter-sensitization phase with daily ayahuasca (100 or 300 mg/kg) or saline (days 19-26), saline challenge (day 30), and ethanol challenge for reinstatement (day 32).

setup_habituation.evidence: Sixty-six mice were given a 10-min habituation period in the open field on 2 consecutive days

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals were individually exposed to the open field arena (freely moving)

food_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum in home cages; no food in the open field apparatus

water_restriction.evidence: Food and water were available ad libitum in home cages; no water in the open field apparatus

time_to_assay.evidence: Ethanol sessions: 5 min after injection; ayahuasca counter-sensitization sessions: 30 min after injection; saline and ethanol challenges 4 and 6 days after last counter-sensitization dose

sample_size.evidence: Six groups of animals were formed (n = 11 for each group)

outcomes.summary: Repeated ethanol (1.8 g/kg, alternate days) induced behavioral sensitization (increased locomotion on day 17 vs day 3). An 8-day repeated treatment with ayahuasca (100 or 300 mg/kg) did not alter locomotor activity per se. Counter-sensitization with ayahuasca (both doses) blocked the reinstatement of ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization upon an ethanol challenge.
outcomes.statistics: Sensitization: time x treatment interaction F(5,60)=2.70, p<0.05. Counter-sensitization phase: no significant effects. Ethanol challenge: pre-treatment x counter-sensitization interaction F(2,60)=4.95, p<0.01; Tukey Eth-Sal > Eth-Aya100 and Eth-Aya300.
outcomes.evidence: Counter-sensitization with ayahuasca at both doses was effective in blocking the expression of the reinstatement of ethanol-induced behavioral sensitization.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Sensitization paradigm without explicit learning task scored

D1_continuity.evidence: Recordings on day 2 (baseline), day 3, day 17, days 19-26 (counter-sensitization), day 30 (saline challenge), day 32 (ethanol challenge)

D3_recording_days.evidence: Baseline (day 2), sensitization days 3 and 17, counter-sensitization 8 consecutive days (days 19-26), saline challenge (day 30), ethanol challenge (day 32)

D4_baseline.evidence: Basal locomotor activity was measured on day 2

D5_followup.evidence: Four days after the last counter-sensitization day (30th day)... Two days after the Saline challenge (day 32)

judge_notes: Both candidates identified the open field as the testing apparatus. GPT-OSS split Experiment 1 into three assays (spontaneous, acute ethanol, sensitization); these are the same paradigm in the same apparatus with the same measure (locomotion frequency) at different timepoints/conditions, so collapsed into a single Experiment 1 assay per rubric decision rule.

Kept Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 as separate assays since the protocols and recording-day structures are substantially different (single vs multi-injection sensitization; counter-sensitization is unique to Exp 2).
Used GLM's correct food/water_restriction = 'during' (open field has no food/water) rather than GPT-OSS's 'not_reported'.
Set time_to_assay = 'multiple' for both assays since recordings occur at varied intervals from drug administration (5 min post-ethanol, 30 min post-ayahuasca, days later for challenges).
